CANONICAL_NAME.value: Go runtime deadlock regression fixtures (src/runtime/testdata/testprog/deadlock.go, go1.22.0): SimpleDeadlock, LockedDeadlock, LockedDeadlock2, GoexitDeadlock, InitDeadlock

value.lineage: The Go runtime's own regression programs for its deadlock detector (checkdead(): 'fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!'), kept since Go 1.x and run by runtime/crash_test.go on every release. Each program is a REAL concurrent deadlock -- goroutines blocked on channels/mutexes with no runnable goroutine left -- preserved as the runtime team wrote it; the runtime is the detector, not the fix. The failing programs are not repaired.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: detection of whole-program deadlock in a concurrent runtime

value.built_to: keep the runtime's deadlock detector honest: each program must still be recognised as a deadlock on every release
value.pressure: concurrent programs that block forever; a runtime that must tell 'everyone is waiting' from 'someone is still working'
value.success_means: the runtime aborts with the deadlock diagnosis instead of hanging silently

value.pressure: many actors blocking on each other; no external observer
value.failure_condition: a hung program that never terminates and never explains why

cut.note: the body is a set of STIMULI, not a mechanism: each registered program constructs one blocking topology (every goroutine parked on a select with no cases; the main thread locked to an OS thread and parked; a locked helper plus a parked main; all goroutines exited via Goexit; thread exhaustion under a thread cap; stack overflow; recursive panics) and the harness asserts the runtime's exact fatal message. The detector that turns 'all goroutines are asleep' into a fatal error lives in runtime/proc.go, outside the body. No organ can be cut; the pressure the fixtures define is recorded

pressures.condition: an organism schedules goroutines onto OS threads; it must detect the global state 'no runnable goroutine and none can be woken by any future event' and abort with a fixed message; near-misses exist: a goroutine locked to a thread and parked (still a deadlock), pending timers (not a deadlock), cgo calls (detection disabled), a thread cap reached (a different fatal error)
pressures.resource_or_constraint: a constant-time check at idle transitions
pressures.failure_condition: a false deadlock report while a timer or external event could still wake a goroutine, or a missed report (the program hangs silently)
pressures.world_punishes: counting only runnable goroutines; ignoring locked threads; ignoring timers
pressures.world_rewards: a check over idle and spinning thread counts plus locked-M accounting, gated off under cgo
pressures.observable_consequence: the seven deadlock programs must each abort with the exact string 'fatal error: all goroutines are asleep - deadlock!' (or the Goexit variant), and the non-deadlock programs must not; the harness reads the first line of output
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a watchdog timeout (which reports late and cannot distinguish slow from stuck)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism told which programs deadlock must reproduce the harness's verdicts exactly; a runtime with the locked-thread accounting removed must miss LockedDeadlock / LockedDeadlock2 (the fixtures exist because it once did); a runtime that ignores timers must false-alarm on a program sleeping in time.Sleep: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: regression fixtures for the Go runtime's deadlock detector (Go authors 2015-)
